children: A federal jury in Tampa, Florida, has awarded airplane component maker Aerosonic nearly $116.9 million after finding that air taxi company Joby Aero broke a confidentiality agreement and misused trade secrets related to Aerosonic aircraft sensors.

The jury in a verdict on Friday found that Joby owes Aerosonic more than $68 million for breaching the companies' non-disclosure agreement and more than $48 million for willfully misappropriating trade secrets related to its air data probes
A Joby spokesperson said on Monday that the company strongly disagrees with the verdict and intends to "vigorously pursue all available post-trial and appellate remedies"
The emerging air-taxi market, led by companies including Joby and backed by major automakers, airlines and investors, has spawned a string of trade-secret and patent disputes

Clearwater, Florida-based Aerosonic sued Joby last year, alleging Joby stole its secrets after Aerosonic sold Joby air data probes and discussed supplying more for its electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft
Santa Cruz, California-based Joby denied the allegations and countersued Aerosonic for allegedly selling it defective probes
The jury also rejected Joby's countersuit on Friday
The case is Aerosonic LLC v. Joby Aero Inc, US District Court for the Middle District of Florida, No. 8:25-cv-00554
For Aerosonic: Todd Tucker of Calfee, Halter & Griswold
For Joby: Naveen Modi of Paul Hastings
